newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends week firmer, resistance pierced.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends week firmer, resistance pierced.

text.p: COMEX copper closed at two-week highs Friday following a late push through resistance levels to brighten up the market's chart outlook, traders said.

A combination of a larger-than-expected fall in LME stocks Friday, and labor tensions at Polish producer KGHM, helped to underpin the market after it weakened earlier in the week to test the 40-day moving average on COMEX and LME, traders said.
"The chart picture shows beautiful support at the 40-day moving average," Rich Hirsch of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.

The bullish factors prompted some fund shortcovering, helped by the realisation that demand was still good in the U.S. The market also shrugged off Fed Chairman Greenspan's clearest warning yet of a rate hike next week, Hirsch added.
May COMEX settled 1.60 cents higher at 112.10 cents a lb, traded 112.60 to 110.40 cents. Spot March went out up 2.75 cents at 118.25 cents.
The spot month settled at its highest level since end of May last year, according to the weekly chart.
Resistance had been pegged by traders around 112.00 cents in the May contract, but the market will also be looking to see if there is any follow-through on Monday.
LME stocks fell 9,675 tonnes to 187,775 tonnes Friday, more than 5,000 tonnes above trader expectations.
The base metals market may well slow down next week ahead of Easter Holidays in the U.S. and Europe, with COMEX shut next Friday.
